Protein digestibility
Protein and amino acid digestibility is a measure of the amount or proportion of dietary protein derived nitrogen and amino acids
that are made available to the organism after digestion and absorption. As the capacity of the small intestinal mucosa to absorb
amino acids, dipeptides, and tripeptides is generally far greater than the amounts in which they are released in the lumen, protein
digestion mainly represents the limiting step in amino acid absorption. Digestibility is determined by measuring the digestive losses
at the level of the terminal ileum or in the feces (Fig. 6).
Fecal and ileal digestibility
Dietary protein-derived nitrogen and/or amino acid absorption is assessed by measuring their disappearance in different part of the
gastrointestinal. The oldest approach determines nitrogen or amino acid absorption by measuring the difference between oral
intake of protein-derived nitrogen or amino acids and nitrogen or amino acids fecal excretion (oro-faecal nitrogen and/or amino
acid disappearance).
